message.reasoning:
I need to decide on an auction bid for Marvin Gardens.

I have $1006 and no monopolies. The current bid is $290, so I need at least $291 to win. I previously thought a $261 bid would deny p3 a yellow group but still leave me with only one path to a yellow monopoly.

I set a $330 cap for the auction. A $291 bid is still safe. If I win, I will hold Atlantic and Marvin as two of three yellow properties. I can then trade for Ventnor. I must not let p2 win this as a trade chip.

Bidding $291 leaves $715 cash, which covers New York and Virginia with a buffer. Even at the $330 cap, $676 remains after the bid. p3 has $829 and can raise further.

p2 has $974 and needs Park Place for a dark blue monopoly. They are using Marvin as a trade chip. p3 can outbid me to the $330 cap with their $829 cash.

I will bid exactly $291. I considered raising to $300 or $310 to signal seriousness, but the minimum is safer.

I am now leaning toward bidding $300 instead of the minimum $291. The other players have been raising by $20 to $30 increments, so a low bid might invite another jump. A $300 bid keeps me competitive while still safely under the $330 cap. It leaves $706 cash, which covers New York and Virginia.

I am now considering raising the bid to $301 or $310. The value of winning Marvin Gardens is limited because p3 already holds Ventnor as the veto and will not trade it for Park Place or St. James.

I realized that if p3 wins the auction, they still cannot complete a yellow monopoly because I hold Atlantic. That property blocks them entirely. The real danger is p2 acquiring Marvin as a trade chip and trading it to p3 for something useful. A trade between p3 and me would be unhelpful since neither player could then build a monopoly.

I will bid $310. This keeps me in the auction and prevents p2 from acquiring Marvin Gardens cheaply as a trade chip.

I am now reconsidering the $310 bid. A $291 minimum bid might be enough, since the other players have been raising by small increments. If they continue bidding, I will reassess next turn.
